title: Per-model limits in the hosted catalog; context budget derived from the model window
acceptance_criteria: Given the hosted catalog, when it is read, then each model has one entry: model id, display name, native context window, maximum output, input, cached-input and cache-write prices, the input price-tier boundary, reasoning levels and token encoding. HOSTED_WINDOW, HOSTED_OUTPUT_TOKENS, PRICES and HOSTED_REASONING_EFFORTS are derived from it or deleted.
Given each hosted model, when its values are recorded, then they are checked against OpenAI's documentation and the source is cited; unverifiable values are flagged, not assumed.

Given any chat model, when a prompt is assembled, then W = min(window − answer reserve − reasoning reserve − safety, price-tier cap), H = min(32K, 25% of W) and E = W − F − H, all computed from that model's catalog entry. HOSTED_WORKING_CONTEXT_TOKENS and its setting are removed.
Given history beyond H, when the chat continues, then compaction and recent-turn selection follow H, so small windows summarise sooner and large windows keep up to 32K verbatim.
Given synthetic catalog entries with X = 16K, 128K and 1M, when answer, planner and compaction prompts are assembled, then every size scales as in the design table and no request exceeds W.
Given a response whose usage reports cached input tokens, when cost is computed (ARA-085 meter, budget ledger), then cached tokens are priced at the cached-input rate from the catalog.
Given /models and the context meter, when they render, then the total is W for the selected model and the native window appears as secondary text, both from the catalog.
test_cases: Catalog completeness; derived views; an unknown model raises as today.
Budget derivation at X = 16K, 128K and 1M; the price-tier cap; history H scaling and compaction thresholds.
verification: Planned on 2026-10-10; revised to derive budgets from X per docs/plans/retrieval-orchestration.md. Branch feat/ara-093-hosted-catalog.
